verdicts.title: BISR runtime keeps n_steps-1 gradient-sized buffers, contradicting the documented p-1-vector / PRNG-replay design
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. _bisr.py:198-211 hands the DENSE length-n_steps recovered strategy coefficients to inverse_as_streaming_matrix; _toeplitz.py:239-244 sizes the forward-substitution state as (bands-1, *grad_shape) with bands = coef.shape[0] = n_steps. Measured on this tree (uv run): grad of 10k floats, n_steps=128 -> state shape (127,10000); n_steps=512 -> (511,10000). At 200k params: n=256 -> 204 MB state, 0.055 s/step; n=1024 -> 818 MB state, 0.411 s/step. Both memory and per-step time scale linearly in n_steps, so a 1B-param, 10k-step run would need tens of TB of noise state. The banded inverse (p coefficients) is available in the same method (inv[:n_steps] is already passed as the row-norm hint), so a p-1-buffer convolution over past iid draws is directly implementable; the sibling lambda-CGD strategy (bandwidth 2) already does exactly the documented PRNG-replay thing (_lambda_cgd.py:143-150 raises NotImplementedError for streaming_matrix and dispatches to _make_lambda_cgd_noise), which makes BISR the anomaly rather than a repo-wide design choice. docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md:10, :47, :96, :109 all promise p-1 noise vectors / PRNG replay. Released noise is numerically correct, so this is a scalability + documentation-contract defect, not a privacy one. No open tracked issue covers BISR runtime memory (#319 is a DP-FTRL invariants umbrella predating this code path; #417 is about benchmark harnesses).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: BISR noise state is (n_steps-1, *grad_shape) instead of the documented (p-1, *grad_shape). Verified: 200k-param gradient, bandwidth=4 -> 204 MB state and 0.055 s per noise step at n_steps=256; 818 MB and 0.411 s at n_steps=1024, i.e. exactly linear in n_steps. Any realistic LLM horizon (n_steps in the thousands, hundreds of millions of parameters) needs terabytes of noise state and O(n_steps*d) work per step, so BISR OOMs long before it is usable, while docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md tells the user memory is p-1 vectors. The released noise itself is correct.

verdicts.title: lr_schedule is compare=False, so the accountant's structural merge collapses MF mechanisms with different schedules
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. lr_schedule is declared field(default=None, compare=False) on all four schedule-carrying strategies (_band_mf.py:110, _bisr.py:160, _blt.py:132, _lambda_cgd.py:119), which excludes it from both __eq__ and __hash__ of the frozen dataclasses. MfGaussian stores the strategy object (_mf_gaussian.py:41-56) and DpProcess.__or__ merges by structural equality (_base.py:473-477). Executed: lambda_cgd_strategy(lambda_=0.5, lr_schedule=cosine) == lambda_cgd_strategy(lambda_=0.5, lr_schedule=constant) == lambda_cgd_strategy(lambda_=0.5) -> all True, hashes equal; per_step(balls_in_bins(mf_gaussian(1.0, s_cos), num_bins=4, n_steps=8)) == the constant-schedule twin -> True; (pa | pb) -> Repeated(count=2) built on pa's cosine leaf. The schedules genuinely price differently: epsilon_at(delta=1e-5) = 3.5374 (cosine) vs 3.6750 (constant). strategy_cache_key DOES distinguish them (verified), so only the equality/hash identity path is blind. lr_schedule was added by #529 (0baaba7a, Aug 2026) with compare=False from the start; open issue #319 predates that code and is a broad DP-FTRL-invariants umbrella, so this is not a duplicate. Severity medium rather than high: it only bites when a user composes MF phases with different schedules under one Accountant, and the sign of the error depends on which schedule comes first.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Two MF processes that differ only in lr_schedule compare and hash equal, so DpProcess.__or__ merges them into Repeated(first_leaf, 2) and prices every step under the first phase's schedule-weighted Gram. Verified on this tree with lambda-CGD + balls_in_bins(num_bins=4, n_steps=8): the two leaves have true epsilons 3.5374 (cosine) and 3.6750 (constant) at delta=1e-5, yet compare equal and merge. A user who composes a cosine-schedule phase then a constant-schedule phase in one accountant is charged entirely at the cosine price, understating the cost. A strategy with no schedule at all also compares equal to one with a schedule.

verdicts.title: Noise-stream continuity tests cover only 2 of 7 noise-state shapes; trainer-level resume test still checks only step count and epsilon
verdicts.reasoning: Verified the coverage gap directly: TestNoiseStreamContinuity in packages/opaque-transformers/tests/opaque_transformers/test_checkpoint_helpers.py has exactly two cases, test_gaussian_noise_continues_after_resume (line 283) and test_band_mf_noise_continues_after_resume (line 289). test_dpftrl_trainer_smoke.py:291-298 asserts only out2.global_step == out1.global_step and privacy_epsilon approx-equality across all six mechanism parametrizations - neither is sensitive to noise-state restoration. I searched the rest of the tree: the only other MF-noise 'resume' assertion is test_noise_addition.py:196-212, which re-calls noise_fn on the same in-memory state and never round-trips through state_dict, and no dpftrl test serializes an MFNoiseState or SecondMomentMFNoiseState. I also confirmed the reporter's claim that there is no live defect: a state_dict -> torch.save -> torch.load -> from_state_dict resume at step 3 of 6 reproduces the uninterrupted draws bit-exactly for identity, band_mf, blt, bisr, bsr and lambda_cgd. So this is regression protection only. Not a duplicate of #538 (test restructuring) or #348 (mechanism-to-accountant conformance).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No current miscomputation: noise-stream continuity across checkpoint/resume is bit-exact today for all six MF strategies (verified by execution). The defect is missing regression coverage - BLT, BISR, BSR, lambda-CGD, identity and the paired second-moment state have no continuity test, and the trainer resume test only compares global_step and epsilon. A future change to BLT buffer serialization, the BISR streaming state, or lambda-CGD key derivation could silently reset or fork the noise stream on resume and no test would fail.

verdicts.title: Loss-scale backoff/growth is an unaccounted data-dependent adaptive choice the docs claim is fully accounted
verdicts.reasoning: Every link checked in source. (1) ClippingStats.all_finite (_clipped_fun.py:73, computed by _all_finite at :98 and aggregated at :439-442/:481) is the raw, un-noised finiteness bit over the batch's pre-clipping per-example gradients - explicitly documented at _clipped_grad.py:165-169 as 'measured after pre_clipping_transform and before clipping sanitizes NaN/Inf'. (2) LossScaler.update (_loss_scaler.py:185-195) consumes that raw bit and multiplies the scale by backoff_factor / growth_factor, so scale_{t+1} = f(private data at step t). (3) clip_pytree (_pytree.py:520-527) nan_to_num's non-finite per-example gradients to zero before clipping, so which records contribute at all is a function of the scale. Hence under add-or-remove adjacency a single record's presence at step t can flip the scale from t+1 on, and with a different scale a different set of records is zeroed, so the released sums for the two neighbouring runs differ by more than the accounted C. That adaptivity flows through a private bit, not through a released output, so per-step PLD composition does not cover it. (4) The docs push exactly this wiring (precision.md:99) and now describe the overflow path as fully 'noised, optimized, and composed into the accountant' (:102-106); 18f67eac deleted the prior 'A skip is data-dependent and is not free privacy-wise' warning and the module docstring's remaining caveat only forbids suppressing the update, not the scale feedback. docs/limitations.md's 'Telemetry outside the guarantee' says to keep such statistics private but says nothing about feeding them back into training. Severity medium, not high: the loss scaler is an opt-in functional-API recipe (DPTrainer does not use it - grep for loss_scaler in opaque-transformers/src is empty), the channel is one bit per step reaching the adversary only indirectly through subsequent releases, and I did not construct a numeric attack. Open issues #383/#322 are alignment/transformers-scoped release-boundary umbrellas and do not cover the engine loss scaler.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: fp16 functional training following docs/user-guide/precision.md: the raw pre-clipping bit stats.all_finite is fed straight into scaler.update, so the loss scale at step t+1 is a function of private data at step t that was never noised or accounted. Because clip_pytree zeroes non-finite per-example gradients, the scale decides which records contribute; two neighbouring datasets that diverge on one overflow event therefore run every subsequent step at different scales and can differ in more than one record's clipped contribution, breaking the per-step sensitivity C that the PLD composition assumes. Reported epsilon is unchanged and is therefore an under-estimate of the composed mechanism. The docs assert the overflow path is fully composed into the accountant and the previous data-dependence warning was removed in 18f67eac.

verdicts.title: The #352 wrapper-blindness pattern survives in unscale_grads and global_norm (silent no-op / silent 0.0 on ClippedPytree)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced by execution. loss_scaler(init_scale=4.0).unscale_grads(clipped({'g': tensor([8.0])}, max_norm=1.0), state) returns the identical ClippedPytree object with 8.0 untouched (unscale_grads at _loss_scaler.py:172-183 uses opaque.pytree.tree_map, which is bare optree - pytree.py:126-142 - and ClippedPytree/NoisedPytree are plain frozen dataclasses never registered as pytree nodes, so they are opaque leaves failing the isinstance(t, torch.Tensor) test). opaque.pytree.global_norm(clipped({'g': tensor([3.0,4.0])}, max_norm=1.0)) returns tensor(0.) versus tensor(5.) on the unwrapped tree, because tree_leaves (pytree.py:122-123) filters to torch.Tensor and finds none. The asymmetry with the #352 fix is real: all_finite in the same module explicitly unwraps ClippedPytree / NoisedPytree / SecondMomentClippingOutput (_loss_scaler.py:220-235) and correctly returns False on a wrapped inf. Both wrong-usage paths fail open with no exception. Severity low and epsilon-neutral: the misuse degrades utility (everything clips) or produces a misleading log, but never reduces the noise or raises the sensitivity, and the documented wiring (unscale as pre_clipping_transform) is correct.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: unscale_grads and global_norm treat the DP wrapper types as opaque leaves. Verified: unscale_grads(ClippedPytree, state) with scale=4 returns the same object with the 8.0 leaf unchanged, and global_norm(ClippedPytree with leaves [3,4]) returns 0.0 instead of 5.0. A user following the torch.amp.GradScaler mental model who calls scaler.unscale_grads on the ClippedPytree returned by grad_fn silently keeps scaled-loss gradients clipped at C (near-100% clipping, badly degraded utility), and a user logging global_norm on clipped grads reads a constant 0.0. Neither raises. all_finite in the same module handles the wrappers correctly, so the inconsistency is within one file.

verdicts.title: Empty-batch short-circuit ignores dtype= and pre_clipping_transform structure, breaking step-shape stability under Poisson sampling
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced both halves. _empty_batch_response (_clipped_grad.py:216-256) builds the zero gradient with zero_grads_like(args, argnums_tuple) (_helpers.py:76-86 = tree_map(torch.zeros_like, params)), which copies the parameter pytree's structure and dtype and applies neither the configured output dtype nor pre_clipping_transform. Executed: bf16 params with dtype=torch.float32 give torch.float32 on a non-empty batch and torch.bfloat16 on an empty one; pre_clipping_transform=lambda g: {'q': g['w']} gives keys ['q'] on a non-empty batch and ['w'] on an empty one. I also traced the downstream consequence: MF noise built on the transformed template raises ValueError('dictionary key mismatch...') on the empty step, while gaussian_noise silently accepts the wrong structure and emits a noised pytree with the wrong keys. adaptive_clipped_grad repeats the same short-circuit at _adaptive.py:402-415. No test pins empty-batch dtype or structure (test_clipped_grad.py's empty-batch tests only check zeros/stats). Severity low: it needs one of two optional knobs (dtype= or a structure-changing pre_clipping_transform) together with an empty Poisson batch, the structure case fails loudly under MF noise, and nothing about sensitivity or noise scale changes, so epsilon is unaffected.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: With dtype= set or a structure-changing pre_clipping_transform, empty Poisson batches return a ClippedPytree whose dtype/structure differs from every non-empty step. Verified: dtype=torch.float32 with bf16 params -> fp32 on non-empty steps, bf16 on empty ones; pre_clipping_transform renaming 'w'->'q' -> keys ['q'] non-empty, ['w'] empty. Downstream, MF noise whose state was built from the transformed template raises ValueError on the empty step, and gaussian_noise silently returns a noised pytree keyed by the untransformed names, which then mismatches optimizer state. adaptive_clipped_grad and auto_clipped_grad share the same short-circuit.
